assignment.name: Week 7 Secure In-class Project Progress Presentation & Demo (8%)

rubric.description: Consistency and Quality of Presentation Contents (30%)
rubric.long_description:
Covers key and relevant parts consistent with the project (as reported in the weekly reports and discussion with the tutor)



1) Overview of the project goals, stakeholders and scope



2) System specification including summary of functional and non-functional requirements, examples of representative user stories, technical constraints, initial system design/architecture, an



3) Quality of work including testing plan, acceptance criteria /tests, adopted acceptance techniques and use an application of discipline knowledge and/or project discipline knowledge or technology (e.g., computer science, advanced computer science, software development/engineering, data science/analytics, robotics, drones)



4) Plan for remaining requirements/user stories and potential project risks



5) Group processes including collaboration and roles, client interaction and potential improvements

ratings.long_description: The project presentation provides excellent and professional elaboration and in-depth clear explanations on all the key and relevant aspects and fully addresses and covers all the criteria including the overview of project goals, system specification, Quality of Work, Plan, Group processes.

The project presentation clearly explains and addresses substantial majority of the  criteria or meets all the criteria but with some ambiguity. Criteria including the overview of project goals, system specification, Quality of Work, Plan, Group processes.

The project presentation generally explains and meets some of the criteria but missing out OR/AND not clearly addressing/shallow explanations on some of the criteria including the overview of project goals, system specification, Quality of Work, Plan, Group processes.

The project presentation gives brief or shallow explanations on some criteria but lacking/missing  proper explanations OR/AND there are flaws in the explanation of the criteria including overview of project goals, system specification, Quality of Work, Plan, Group processes.

The project presentation only includes and briefly explains a few of the criteria but missing out a major portion OR/AND there are flaws in the explanation of the criteria:
covers key and relevant parts (Overview of project goals, system specification, Quality of Work, Plan, Group processes); or the majority of the contents generated by AI.

rubric.long_description:
o   whether the presentation is logically and professionally structured, well planned to guide the audiences to capture the important contents;
o   whether the presentation makes professional use of appropriate tools (texts, tables, pictures, animation, etc.) - easy to follow, consistent and professional styles, well-balanced highlights and details - not too much text, and be clear and professional

o   whether all the presenters are confident and well-prepared (not reading from notes/mobile ...)
o   whether the appropriate body language and eye contacts are used
o   whether the expression is clear with appropriate volume throughout the entire presentation
o   whether the presentation can attract and hold audiences attention and be efficiently and effectively delivered within the time limits

ratings.long_description:
The project presentation clearly explains and meets all the criteria: covers key and relevant parts
Presentation excellent time management; all sections of the presentation are well-timed and contribute to a coherent overall flow.
The presentation structure is perfectly logical and effectively guides the audience through the project.
Presentation is very well rehearsed and can attract and hold the attentions of the audiences throughout the entire presentation. All the presenters are confident and never merely read from slides, and always have appropriate eye contact with audiences, and proper use of body language.

The project presentation clearly explains and meets most of the criteria: covers key and relevant parts
Presentation good time management; most sections of the presentation are well-timed and contribute to a coherent overall flow.
The presentation structure is good, logical, and effectively guides the audience through the project.
Presentation is well rehearsed and can attract and hold the attentions of the audiences throughout the entire presentation. Only one presenter or two presenters may be not confident enough and glance at their slides a few times, yet mostly with eye contact with audiences.

The project presentation clearly explains and meets the criteria. Some key and relevant parts are missing.
Time management is generally acceptable. Most sections are within a reasonable time range, but some parts may feel slightly rushed or too long. Overall flow is maintained, but not optimal.
The structure is generally clear. Group members are not confident enough and read from their slides many times, or may have no eye contacts with audience, no body language.

Some of the keys and relevant parts are missing.
Most parts may feel rushed or too long.
The structure is generally clear but may lack coherence or smooth transitions between sections. Some parts are disjointed or not logically ordered. All presenters are not confident enough and mainly read from their slides.

Lack of some keys and relevant parts.
The whole presentation is rushed or too long.
The structure is not clear and hard to follow.
Most presenters are not confident enough and constantly read from their slides during the presentation.

rubric.long_description:
o   whether the group can inspire discussions with the audiences (other groups);
o   whether the group members give sensible answers or ask meaningful questions that show understanding of the work done
1) convening and sensible answers and questions that show understanding of the work done
2) Answer all the questions.
3) Every member should be able to answer general questions about the project
4) Every member should be able to answer their respective technical question without delegation

ratings.long_description:
The group responses clearly cover and meet all Q&A  criteria:
sensible answers, answer all questions in professional manner, answer both general and technical questions without delegation; all members actively participates in the Q&A session and provides professional response to the questions.

The group responses  meet MOST of the Q&A criteria:
the group is able to provide sensible answers, answers substantial majority of the questions as a group. However, there may be one presenter does not participate in Q&A session.

The group's responses meet some of the Q&A criteria but misses out OR/AND not clearly mentioned the following criteria. The group does not provide sensible answers, to some questions or up to 2 presenters don't actively participate Q&A session and delegate other members to help on Q&A.

The group's responses have major issues and marginally meets Q&A  criteria.
The group manages to make sensible answers to some of  questions, some members (up to 3 members in a main stream unit) don't actively participate Q&A or their answers are not sensible or not professional.

The group's responses do not meet most of the Q&A criteria and/or major issues: the group cannot provide sensible answers to a number of questions; the a number of group members cannot answer questions related to their tasks or don't actively participate Q&A session at all.
